title: Williams Agrees to Buy Momentum Midstream for $5.5 Billion
summary: Williams Cos. reached a deal to buy Momentum Midstream LLC from the private equity firm EnCap Flatrock Midstream through a deal valued up to $5.5 billion, expanding its natural gas network along the US Gulf Coast.

title: Yen Holds Steady in US Hours After Speculation of Intervention
summary: The yen held steady through the New York trading session on Monday, after a sharp advance earlier in the day that sparked speculation authorities may have intervened to support the currency again after last week’s coordinated action between the US and Japan.

title: Korean Firms Expanded Short-Term Debt Funding Before Market Rout
summary: South Korean financial companies and other firms borrowed more money in short-term debt markets in the first half of the year amid an unprecedented stock market rally that gave way to a meltdown in recent weeks.

title: Emerging-Market Currencies Trade Mixed as US-Iran Tensions Ease
summary: Emerging-market currencies were mixed on Monday as investors weighed signs of easing tensions between the US and Iran against the fading appeal for carry trades in Latin America.

title: Trump Family-Linked Bitcoin Miner Posts Second-Quarter Loss
summary: American Bitcoin Corp., the Trump family-backed miner launched last year just before the cryptocurrency tumbled from record highs, posted a third consecutive quarterly loss after a decline in the value of its holdings.

title: Treasuries Climb to Start Week on Oil, Bessent’s Yen Pledge
summary: Treasuries are starting the week on an optimistic note, buoyed by tumbling oil prices and assurances that tens of billions of dollars in Japanese currency interventions won’t be funded from sales of US government debt.

summary: Gold fluctuated as traders weighed the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path after cooling tensions in the Middle East eased energy-driven inflation.

title: Fund Launches and Leveraged ETFs Flood The Industry | ETF IQ 8/3/2026
summary: "Bloomberg ETF IQ" focuses on the opportunities, risks and current trends tied to the trillions of dollars in the global exchange traded funds industry. Today's guests: Vident Asset Management President Amrita Nandakumar, Matthews CIO & Portfolio Manager Sean Taylor, Amplify ETFs Founder & CEO Christian Magoon, and Capital Group Head of Global Product Strategy and Development Holly Framsted.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iran War Risk Still Important in Background, Says Torsten Slok
summary:
Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo, said that while AI and the Fed may be issues more at the forefront of the economic conversation, risk from the Iran war and its subsequent impact on fuel stores remains an important factor in the background. 
Slok also commented the possibility that the Fed may have fewer meetings, saying that market will still try to price the Fed regardless of the schedule.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Talks Are Iran’s ‘Last Chance’ Says Trump (Full Q&A)
summary: President Donald Trump said his latest offer of talks is a “last chance” for Iran after he called off what he said was a major attack on the Islamic Republic.  “I want to give them every last chance before decapitation,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “You’ll find out today or tomorrow. I mean, they’re going to go quickly, one way or the other. It’s not very complex.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japan’s Use of Fed Tool Could Test Yen Resolve, Evercore Says
summary: A rarely used Federal Reserve liquidity facility could prevent the Japanese from selling Treasuries to prop up the yen, but prolonged use of the tool could encourage markets to test the US and Japan’s resolve, according to Evercore ISI.

title: Active ETF, Model Portfolio Growth to Persist: Framsted
summary: Holly Framsted, head of global product strategy and development at Capital Group, joins Scarlet Fu and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." They discussed ETF and mutual funds flows as well as allocation shifts within model portfolios. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Slips as Trump Says Iran, US in Talks Over Hormuz Reopening
summary: Oil fell after both the US and Iran signaled that discussions to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz are ongoing, raising hopes for a pickup in supply from the Middle East.

title: Senators Urge CFTC to Curb Wildfire Prediction Market Bets Over Arson Concerns
summary: A group of Democratic senators urged the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to rein in prediction market trading on wildfires, expressing concern that individuals could be tempted to commit arson to make their bets pay off.

title: Corgi On Pace to Launch 500 ETFs In First Year
summary:
Bloomberg's Isabelle Lee joins Scarlet Fu and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." Corgi is on pace to launch roughly 500 ETFs within its first year, more than BlackRock accumulated over many years. It already ranks among the largest US issuers by product count and says its eventual goal is 1,000 funds spanning leveraged stocks, buffered strategies, semiconductors and narrowly targeted themes.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Banks Offload Risk from Leveraged ETFs with ‘Crash Puts’
summary:
Bloomberg's Yiqin Shen joins Scarlet Fu and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." Leveraged ETFs that offer the tantalizing prospect of doubling or tripling the daily returns of an individual stock are famously risky for investors who buy them. The result has been a quiet surge of activity in an exotic corner of the derivatives market, where investment banks, hedge funds and other institutional investors trade what are often known as “crash puts” and sometimes referred to as cliquets or stability notes.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Back and Forth on Iran Confused Everyone in Region, Says Michael Allen
summary: Michael Allen, managing director of Beacon Global Strategies and a former national security aide to President George W. Bush, said that America's inability to stick to a coherent message on Iran has confused the American people and the MidEast region, including US adversaries. Allen also discussed the tentative agreement to rebuild Gaza, saying there is a low likelihood that it is enacted how it looks on paper but that the President and his team deserve credit for trying.  (Source: Bloomberg)
